topStories.headline: Soldier Hollow Locks In Three-Year UCI Mountain Bike World Cup Commitment After Debut Draws 9,000 Fans
topStories.dek: The Utah Olympic Legacy Foundation announced October 1 that the WHOOP UCI Mountain Bike World Cup will return to Midway in 2027 and 2028 after the September debut at Soldier Hollow exceeded expectations.
topStories.body:
Soldier Hollow Nordic Center in Midway will host the WHOOP UCI Mountain Bike World Cup in 2027 and 2028, the Utah Olympic Legacy Foundation announced October 1. The 2027 event is set for September 25–26. The commitment follows the venue's debut as a World Cup stop on September 19–20, which drew more than 9,000 spectators over the two-day weekend.

The 2026 edition featured UCI cross-country Olympic and cross-country short track World Cup races for elite men, elite women, and under-23 fields, as well as a high school mountain bike race on Saturday afternoon. On the elite women's side, Martina Berta of Origine Racing Division swept both the XCC and XCO races — a feat only ten other women had accomplished in a single World Cup weekend. Elite men's XCO honors went to Martín Vidaurre of Specialized Factory Racing, who launched a decisive final-lap attack to win. Local favorite Haley Batten, the Paris 2024 Olympic silver medalist who trains at Soldier Hollow, finished sixth in the women's XCO race.

Soldier Hollow venue manager Melanie Welch said in a statement that the turnout and energy from spectators were outstanding, and that the venue looks forward to hosting the event for three years. The Midway venue, which hosted Olympic biathlon and cross-country skiing in 2002, was one of only three North American stops on the 2026 World Series circuit.

The multi-year commitment cements Heber Valley's place on the international mountain bike racing calendar through at least 2028 and builds on the area's Olympic legacy infrastructure in ways that local tourism and economic development officials say will benefit the broader Wasatch County community.

topStories.headline: Former Wasatch County Sheriff's Office Administrator Pleads Guilty to Felony Sex Charge
topStories.dek: Mitchell McKee, 61, entered a guilty plea September 29 to one count of unlawful sexual activity with a minor; original ten felony charges were dismissed and sentencing is set for November 10.
topStories.body:
Former Wasatch County Sheriff's Office administrator Mitchell McKee, 61, pleaded guilty on Monday, September 29, to one count of unlawful sexual activity with a minor, a third-degree felony, the Park Record reported. The original ten felony sex crimes charges against McKee were dismissed as part of the plea agreement.

Fourth District Court Judge Anthony Howell accepted the plea, noting that the decision did not come easily. The maximum penalty for the third-degree felony is up to five years in prison, a $5,000 fine, and mandatory registration as a sex offender. McKee remains in custody pending a sentencing hearing scheduled for November 10.

The original charges, which were dropped when McKee agreed to the plea deal, included two first-degree felony counts of human trafficking of a child, two first-degree felony counts of forcible sodomy, one first-degree felony count of enticing a minor, two second-degree felony counts of forcible sexual abuse, two second-degree felony counts of sexual exploitation of a minor, and one count of dealing in materials harmful to a minor.

McKee was arrested in March 2024 after Heber City police identified him as a suspect in a sex crimes investigation that began around December 2023. He had also worked as a sex therapist in Provo before his employment in administrative services at the Sheriff's Office.

topStories.headline: Heber Valley Temple Case Heads Into Final Legal Chapter as Utah Supreme Court Weighs Ruling
topStories.dek: After oral arguments before the state's highest court on September 4, Wasatch County residents await a final ruling on whether the county's approval of the LDS temple was lawful — a decision observers say could reshape zoning law across Utah.
topStories.body:
The Utah Supreme Court heard oral arguments on September 4 in Van Dusen v. Wasatch County, the long-running lawsuit challenging Wasatch County's approval of the Heber Valley Utah Temple. The justices have not yet issued a final decision on the underlying appeal, leaving the community in a holding pattern that could end at any time.

The dispute centers on whether Wasatch County lawfully used a legislative development agreement to approve the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' plans for an 88,000-square-foot, three-story temple on an 18.17-acre site just east of Heber City. A group of nearby Red Ledges-area residents filed the original lawsuit in 2023, arguing the approval violated local zoning rules and state law. The Fourth District Court dismissed the case, but the residents appealed to the Supreme Court.

In February 2026, the Supreme Court allowed construction to proceed during the appeal, finding the plaintiffs had not demonstrated irreparable harm from continued work. Since then, reinforced concrete basement walls have been rising at the site and twenty dewatering wells have been managing the area's high water table. Two justices — Associate Chief Justice Jill Pohlman and Justice Jay Jorgensen — are recused; two district court judges are sitting by designation in their places.

Plaintiff Bruce Van Dusen said ahead of the September 4 arguments that the outcome will shape how every Utah property owner thinks about the predictability of zoning laws. No date has been announced for the court's final opinion, but once issued it will either affirm Wasatch County's approval or potentially require construction to halt and the site to be restored.

events.title: Midway Farmers Market — Final Weeks of the Season
events.location: Midway Town Square, 200 West Main Street, Midway
events.description: The market runs every Saturday through Halloween, its final day of the 2026 season. The October 31 closing will include trunk-or-treating for kids alongside nearly 30 vendors offering local produce, eggs, baked goods, flowers, and artisan goods.

events.title: Pumpkin Train at Heber Valley Railroad
events.location: Heber Valley Railroad Depot, 450 S 600 W, Heber City
events.description: The 40-minute family ride departs Saturdays (Oct. 3, 10, 17, 24) with on-board entertainment, a pumpkin chocolate-chip cookie, and a pumpkin from the patch to take home. General admission is $15 for ages 2 and up; tickets at hebertrain.com.

events.title: Halloween Express at Heber Valley Railroad
events.location: Heber Valley Railroad Depot, 450 S 600 W, Heber City
events.description: A 90-minute family-friendly evening train to Grim Hollow station runs Mondays, Thursdays, and Fridays throughout October. The Witches Night Out option offers table-car seating with tea service and Halloween desserts on the same train.

events.title: Fall Festival at Kohler Creamery
events.location: Heber Valley Artisan Milk & Cheese (Kohler Creamery), 920 River Rd, Midway
events.description: Open Monday through Saturday through the end of October, the festival on this working dairy farm features a hay maze, slides, bounce houses, corn pits, yard games, and pumpkins; haunted hayrides run Thursday through Saturday evenings.

events.title: Annual Utah Tourism Conference
events.location: Grand Hyatt Deer Valley, 1702 Glencoe Mountain Way, Heber City
events.description: The state's premier tourism industry gathering brings professionals from across Utah to Heber Valley to network and learn. Registration is open at gohebervalley.com.

events.title: Candidate Forum: Wasatch County Council & Utah House District 59
events.description: KPCW and the Heber Leadership Academy are co-hosting this free public forum for candidates running for Utah House District 59 and Wasatch County Council Seats A, C, and F. The event will be livestreamed on KPCW; mail-in ballots go out October 13.

events.title: Heber Halloween Fest
events.location: Heber City Main Street Park, 250 S Main Street, Heber City
events.description: Free trick-or-treating, a spook alley, carnival, food trucks, and live entertainment including performances by Stomp It Out Dance Studio and the Intensity Dance Team's Thriller routine. Carnival wristbands are $10 per person or $40 per family.

moreNews.headline: Wasatch County Explores Returning Excess Tax Revenue Directly to Property Owners
moreNews.body: Wasatch County is weighing a program that would direct excess general fund revenue back to property owners as targeted tax relief, the Park Record reported September 29. County administrators worked with the offices that collect property taxes to identify the opportunity after many Heber Valley homeowners saw assessments rise sharply alongside climbing home values. No vote has been scheduled yet; the County Council is expected to discuss details in coming weeks.

moreNews.headline: Four Dog-Waste Stations Installed on Heber Trails; Seven More Await Council Dog-Policy Decision
moreNews.body: The Community Alliance for Main Street installed four new dog-waste stations along the Red Ledges Center Street and Humbug paved trails this fall, funded by a $2,900 Wasatch County TAP Tax award and a $1,000 Utah Division of Water Quality grant, KPCW reported October 1. Seven additional stations planned for Heber City parks will be sited only after the Heber City Council makes a final decision on the town's broader dog policy, a question expected at an October council meeting.

hotels.name: Rivers Edge Resort at Heber Valley

shops.name: Inspiration Haven Art Studio

artEntertainment.name: Avon Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A beloved Heber City landmark since 1948, the Avon Theatre screens a curated mix of current releases and classics; open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.

artEntertainment.name: Soldier Hollow Nordic Center
artEntertainment.type: Olympic Nordic venue and events center

artEntertainment.description: Located at the Heber Valley Airport, this museum houses a significant collection of WWII aircraft, authentic artifacts, uniforms, armament, and women-in-aviation memorabilia.

artEntertainment.name: Daughters of the Utah Pioneers Museum
artEntertainment.description: A Heber City museum preserving the history of the area's pioneer settlers and early Wasatch Valley communities.

artEntertainment.name: Wasatch Mountain State Park Golf Courses
artEntertainment.description: Wasatch Mountain State Park offers 36 holes of championship golf plus 18 holes at Soldier Hollow, set amid stunning mountain scenery in Midway.
